vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: lobstercash
Version: 0.0.13

The lobstercash skill bundle provides a comprehensive interface for AI agents to manage crypto wallets, pay for APIs via the x402 protocol, and perform automated web checkouts using virtual cards. The instructions in SKILL.md and the reference files (e.g., purchase.md, cards.md, and send.md) emphasize security and human-in-the-loop (HITL) controls, explicitly requiring user approval via external URLs for all sensitive financial actions. No evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or unauthorized execution was found; instead, the bundle includes detailed anti-patterns to prevent the agent from hallucinating URLs or bypassing user confirmation.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions, requested capabilities, and required inputs are internally consistent with a payment/checkout wallet assistant, but it relies on an external npm CLI and performs highly sensitive actions (card reveal, signing transactions, browser automation) so review the external package and follow the human-approval safeguards before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name and description (buying, sending crypto, virtual cards, browser checkout, x402 payments) match the SKILL.md instructions. All commands and flows (cards request, crypto request, purchase explore/run, tx signing, x402 fetch) are coherent with a payment/wallet skill and no unrelated credentials or binaries are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions include operations with high sensitivity (revealing virtual card numbers/CVC, signing and submitting on-chain transactions, and automated browser checkout that fills forms). Those actions are appropriate for a payments skill, and the document repeatedly mandates human approval and not polling. Pay attention: the agent is instructed to open external approval URLs and to reveal sensitive data after user consent; the SKILL.md includes behavioral requirements (do not poll, confirm user approvals) that should be enforced by the agent runtime.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill bundle itself is instruction-only, but the SKILL.md directs users to install an external npm package (npm install -g @crossmint/lobster-cli) and to update from an external site (https://www.lobster.cash/install). Because the runtime behavior depends on code fetched from npm / the project site, verify the package publisher and package contents before installing. There is no install spec embedded in the skill bundle.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, only documents an optional LOBSTER_AGENT_ID for concurrent sessions. It does not request unrelated credentials or config paths. The amount and types of sensitive access (card reveals, wallet signing) are appropriate for a payments agent.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true, does not modify other skills or system-wide settings in the bundle, and is user-invocable. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default (platform normal), and that increases the importance of the human-approval instructions that the SKILL.md emphasizes.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent for handling purchases, virtual cards, and wallet operations, but it performs very sensitive actions (revealing card numbers, signing transactions, automating browser checkouts) and depends on an external npm CLI (@crossmint/lobster-cli) and lobster.cash endpoints. Before installing or using it: 1) Verify the npm package and publisher (search npmjs.com and the project repo or docs) and confirm the install URL is legitimate; 2) Only follow approval links shown by the CLI yourself — do not allow the agent to auto-approve or poll for consent; 3) Keep virtual card amounts small and prefer single-use cards when possible; 4) Do not share private keys or main card numbers — the flow uses virtual cards and agent wallets, and the SKILL.md instructs to treat revealed credentials as highly sensitive; 5) If you are uncomfortable with an agent having autonomous ability to initiate payments, restrict use to explicit user-invoked actions and monitor approvals; 6) If you want stronger assurance, review the external CLI package source code (or vendor documentation) before installing. If you want, I can help check the npm package and the lobster.cash homepage for ownership, repository links, and known reviews.
llm.findings: [none] expected: No regex scan findings or pre-scan injection signals were detected. However, absence of findings is expected for an instruction-only skill with no code files to analyze.
